Individuals must contact their local library to request an ILL item. ### ISBN South Africa's National Library (NLSA) assigns unique 13-digit ISBNs to books published worldwide. ISBNs identify and track books, and are essential for the book industry. ### Legal Deposit ### Our Facilities/Venue Hire The NLSA offers the Auditorium, Training Room, and Committee Room for hire, all equipped with state-of-the-art technology and audiovisual equipment. ### Photocopying & Scanning The NLSA offers black and white or color photocopying services for library materials and personal documents in A4 or A3 size. Self-service photocopiers are available in the reading rooms. ### Reading Rooms The NLSA has two reading rooms: the General Reading Room, with over one million books and periodicals, and the Abe Bailey Reading Room, with rare and valuable materials. ### Reference The NLSA offers reference desk assistance, workshops, and online resources to help users with referencing. ### Search the Catalogue Search the catalogue to find books, pictures, maps, manuscripts and more or search our digital records. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Latest News - Rhodes University Library Management System Upgrade (https://www.ru.ac.za/library/latestnews/rhodes_university_library_management_system_upgrade-1.html) 【turn376search1】 [wordlim: 200] Crawled: 2 months ago; The Rhodes University Library has just upgraded its management software system from Sierra to ALMA. Jan # Rhodes University Library Management System Upgrade Image: RULIS RULIS The Rhodes University Library has just upgraded its management software system from Sierra to ALMA. As a result, there are a few notable changes that will affect you. Firstly, the Library has started to use OpenAthens as the access management system for its e-resources. OpenAthens provides software which allows users to use a single username and password to access all of the Library’s subscribed content (online databases, journals and e-books). Authentication will be required both on and off campus. Secondly, the Library’s searching interface has been upgraded. In the past Library users relied on two search tools (OPAC and Summon) on the Library’s website in order to find content. As a result of the upgrade users will now only have to rely on using a single search tool (Primo).   If you experience any problems using OpenAthens or Primo please contact Lusanda Nyoka or Thandiwe Menze for assistance. Image: Chest x-ray Medicine and health ## Study assesses diagnostic accuracy of WHO algorithms for childhood TB FMHS Marketing & Communications 27 November 2025 * An estimated 1.2 million children fell ill with TB in 2023, yet less than half received proper diagnosis and treatment. * To address this diagnostic gap, the World Health Organisation (WHO) introduced Treatment Decision Algorithms in 2022. * A new international study, published in PLOS Medicine, provides the first large-scale external validation of these WHO algorithms. In 2023, 10.8 million people fell ill with tuberculosis (TB) and 1.25 million died, confirming TB as the world’s leading infectious disease killer. Among them, an estimated 1.2 million were children, yet less than half received proper diagnosis and treatment. To address this diagnostic gap, the World Health Organisation (WHO) introduced in 2022 Treatment Decision Algorithms (TDAs) — simple, standardised clinical tools designed to help health workers identify children who should start TB treatment, especially in low-resource settings where access to advanced diagnostic tools, such as molecular or imaging tests, remains limited. -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- You made us the benchmark in the sector! | Stellenbosch University (https://www.su.ac.za/en/about/governance/executive-management/operations-and-finance/responsibility-centre/news/you-made-us-benchmark-sector) 【turn376search4】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 11 months ago; Crawled: 5 months ago; Providing 1.2 million meals in 2025 with yet again zero food poisoning incidents is a fantastic achievement but making sure that our students have access to affordable and nutritious meals make you real superheroes on our campus! to “Look, it works!” Your patience and enthusiasm deserve its own award.  With 6 new spinout companies in 2025 and millions of rands in investment raised for our companies, we had a bumper year!  Well done!
